 FROM:  John N. Incontro, Police Chief

 BY:  Robert A. Ocean II, Police Cadet

 DATE:  March 7, 2022

 SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT FEBRUARY 2022

BACKGROUND

Each month, the San Marino Police Department provides a brief and informational update on
crime, traffic issues, and other items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

This report is compiled in order to inform the Public Safety Commission with essential
information regarding the department’s activity in the month of February 2022. The pandemic
has resulted in alternation of police service in our community. The department has had one
neighborhood watch meeting, one business watch meeting and has continued to limit contact
with individuals to lessen the possibility of viral infection. The services at the front desk continue
with caution and require the wearing of face masks.

As of February 31, 2022, Part 1 crimes have had an overall decreased by 28.21% when compared
to February 2021. In February, six larcenies occurred related to thefts from vehicles and
residences. Three residential burglaries occurred in the City along with one attempt burglary.

DETECTIVE BUREAU / INVESTIGATIONS

As of February 28, 2022, the Detective Bureau completed the following activities:

  •  Nine filings were submitted to the district attorney’s office for review
  •  Six cases are still under review by the DA’s office. One of these cases filed was for a
  stolen vehicle recovery.

In February 1, 2022, there were three residential burglaries reported and one attempted
residential burglary reported to the department. Residents were home in three of these
residential burglaries. In one of these burglaries, unknown suspects forced entry into the
residence but fled the location shortly after climbing up towards the second story balcony. The
resident heard the suspects and confronted them. The suspects then fled the location in opposing

  Page 5 of 31
 north/south directions from the location. There was no loss reported during this burglary. In
the other burglary, an unknown suspect forced entry through a window. The suspect was
interrupted by the homeowner. The resident observed the suspect run through the rear door
of the residence. Miscellaneous personal effects were missing from the residence. The residence
has an alarm but the alarm was not activated. In the third burglary, the elderly resident was
unaware of the burglary. A family member arrived home a few hours later and observed two
rear window panes shattered and two bedrooms ransacked. An exterior camera did not capture
the incident. There was no alarm at the residence. The loss was undetermined at this time.

A package theft occurred from the front porch of a residence. The resident was able to describe
a suspect and a suspect vehicle through a doorbell camera at the residence. Officers conducted
an area check and located the vehicle. A traffic enforcement stop was conducted and the victim’s
property was located inside the vehicle. Two occupants inside the vehicle were arrested, cited
and released for the theft.

Our analysis indicates that there is no specific pattern or location selected; however, none of the
homes had a security system or an alarm not activated. The point of entry for the burglary in
most of the incidents was the rear of the home. This information will assist us in our crime
prevention efforts. We have provided the information to residents via the Neighborhood Watch
Block Captains, police department website, e-mail and social media. Additionally, we are working
on a crime suppression strategy to reduce these crimes. We continue to see an overall decrease
in residential burglaries as compared to previous years.

COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT

The department has had two community events occur in the month of February. One event
consisted of a Neighborhood Watch / Disaster Prep meeting and the other was a Business Watch
meeting. The business watch meeting was held via zoom and in person with several business
owners with shops along Mission Street. The business owners provided excellent information
about their needs that will help as our partnership grows.

PERSONNEL

The department currently has 27 of the 30 sworn positions filled. There are three sworn position
vacancies. We are currently processing two lateral police officer applicants. One of them is in the
early stages of the process, while the second is in the final stages of the hiring process. The
department also has two cadet vacancies, and a potential candidate has begun the hiring process.

TECHNOLOGY

The Flock ALPR agreement for nine new cameras will go before City Council on Wednesday,
March 9, 2022. Once City Council approves funding for the additional Flock cameras, Police
Department Staff will move forward with Flock representatives to finalize the agreement and
begin installing the new cameras.

  Page 6 of 31
 The Police Department staff will also be presenting a report at that City Council to move forward
with the purchase of an traffic collision and citation software. This software is part of the
Department’s Office of Traffic Safety grant.

TRAFFIC

Traffic Enforcement

Traffic enforcement is based upon three categories; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list of
traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our traffic
collision investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory factor in
the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.

The traffic data utilized for traffic enforcement are the top locations for traffic collisions and the
top Primary Collision Factors. The patrol division is continuing normal routine traffic
enforcement and patrols.

Below are the top collision locations of February 2022
  1. Huntington Drive – Nine Collisions
  2. Los Robles Ave – Five Collisions
  3. Sierra Madre Boulevard – Two Collisions
  4. Lorain Road – Two Collisions

Below are the top factors of collisions of February 2022
  1. CVC 22107 – Turning and Stopping and Turning Signals – Five Collisions
  2. CVC 22350 – Speeding – Five Collisions
  3. CVC 21800 – Yield Right-of-way at Intersection – Five Collisions
  4. CVC 22450 – Stop Sign / Special Stops – Five Collisions

Moving Violations

The patrol division is continuing maximum efforts in place of the motor officers in answering all
traffic complaints and covering primary collision areas. We continue to utilize the speed radar
trailer and signs to remind motorists of the posted speed limit.

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY REPORT

COVID-19 RESPONSE

San Marino Fire Department personnel continue to follow department personal protective
equipment protocols during emergencies for the safety of firefighters and patients. Additionally,
paramedics follow all current Los Angeles County Department of Health Services protocols for
the evaluation and transportation of patients requiring emergency medical services.

Daily positive case rates have continued to decline in Los Angeles County. EMS Responses in
February averaged 3 per day across all Verdugo agencies compared with 16 per day in January.
66% of COVID patients treated by EMS personnel required transport to a local area hospital.
There were no COVID EMS response in San Marino during the month of February.

On March 4, the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health (DPH) issued a revised health
order to align masking requirements with the State of California’s Public Health Officer Order of
February 28, 2022. Under the revised order, indoor masking is strongly recommended, but no
longer required in most indoor settings. Masking will continue to be required for all persons,
regardless of vaccination status, in high transmission risk settings, like on public transit, health
care settings, correctional facilities, and long-term care centers. Beginning March 12, masks will
continue to be strongly recommended, but not required, in K-12 schools or childcare facilities.
The full Health Order may be viewed on the DPH website.

As of February 27, 2022, 85.6% of San Marino residents age 5 and older have been fully
vaccinated. 59.7% of residents age 12 and older have received a vaccine booster.

EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN TRAINING

The San Marino Fire Department provided training to members of the Executive Team and their
management staff to develop every department’s Emergency Action Plan (EAP). An EAP is a State
mandated written plan that provides procedures for employees during a workplace emergency.
Each department’s EAP includes instructions for emergency notifications, employee assembly
locations, and utility shut off locations. Procedures are provided for multiple potential workplace
emergencies, including fire and medical emergencies, earthquakes, adverse weather events, bomb
threats, and more. As part of the plan development training, staff reviewed potential emergency

  Page 11 of 31
 scenarios such as active shooter events, an earthquake along the Raymond/Sierra Madre/San
Andreas faults, and gas main ruptures along the Garfield Avenue pipeline.

STAFFING

On February 23, the San Marino Fire Department conducted interviews for the position of
Firefighter/Paramedic. Two successful candidates were moved forward to begin the process of
background investigations. There is currently one vacant position.

SIGNIFICANT INCIDENTS

On February 4, 2022, Engine 91 responded with units from the Los Angeles County Fire
Department and the Pasadena Fire Department to a garage fully engulfed in flames. San Marino
Firefighters contained the fire to the garage and nearby vegetation. The quick efforts by the fire
department kept the fire from extending to homes on Homet Road in San Marino.

An extreme weather event on February 15 brought large amounts of hail to parts of Southern
California, including the City of San Marino. The San Marino Fire Department received multiple
calls for assistance, including a report of a downed power line at the intersection of Santa Anita
Avenue and Wallingford Road. Upon arrival on scene, Fire Department personnel utilized a
voltage detector to confirm that the downed wire was energized and carrying an electrical
current. Fire Department personnel established a perimeter around the downed line and
remained on scene until Southern California Edison’s arrival. Downed power lines are extremely
hazardous and can cause severe injury or death. Residents are advised to call 9-1-1 immediately
if they see a downed power line. Always assume that a downed power line is carrying electricity
and maintain a distance of at least 20 feet. Visit Southern California Edison for more power line
safety information.

On February 14, Engine 91 and Battalion 9 responded to a HAZMAT incident on the Caltech
campus after smoke was reported from a lab room. Engine 91 assisted the Pasadena Fire
Department with evacuation of students and faculty.

On February 28, San Marino Engine 91 provided mutual aid assistance to the City of Montebello
while their Fire Department responded to a 3 Alarm apartment house fire. Engine 91 responded
to several incidents in the City of Montebello during their “move up” assignment. RA91 remained
available in the City of San Marino with assistance from South Pasadena Engine 81.

FY 2021-22 DEPARTMENT OBJECTIVES

  •  Continue to lead the City’s response to COVID-19.
  •  Continue to provide accurate measurements of Fire Department performance.
  •  Place into service new Rescue Ambulance 91.
  •  Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  •  Develop a City-wide Evacuation Plan for review and approval by the Disaster Council and
  City Council.

  Page 12 of 31
 •  Improve the City’s Emergency Preparedness through the completion of the upgrade to
  the Emergency Operations Center, including new phone and computer set up, new
  mapping, and staff training.
•  Review and revise the City’s Emergency Operations Plan for City Council adoption.
•  Conduct a City-wide emergency operations exercise with City staff, Department Heads,
  and the School District.
•  Complete necessary upgrades to the Emergency Operations Center in coordination with
  the Parks and Public Works Department.

SUBJECT:  REVIEW OF ORDINANCE NO. O-22-1387 AMENDING THE CITY
  CODE TO ALIGN BOARD AND COMMISSION TERM START
  DATES, DECOMMISSION THE RECREATION COMMISSION, AND
  ADJUST BOARD AND COMMISSION MEETING TIMES

BACKGROUND

On March 9, 2022 the San Marino City Council is scheduled to discuss and potentially approve
Ordinance No. O-22-1387 Amending the City Code to Align Board and Commission Term Start
Dates, Decommission the Recreation Commission, and Adjust Board and Commission Meeting
Times. Should the City Council approve Ordinance No. O-22-1387, the effects to the Public
Safety Commission would be twofold: 1) the date and time of the Public Safety Commission’s
monthly meeting would move from the 1st Monday of the month at 7 PM to the 3rd Monday of
the month at 6 PM; and 2) the start of term date would move from July 1 to June 1.

DISCUSSION

The San Marino City Council is scheduled to vote on Ordinance No. O-22-1387 on March 9,
2022. Two significant changes would be made to the Public Safety Commission should City
Council approve Ordinance No. O-22-1387.

Beginning in January 2022, new submission procedures for City Council staff reports require all
reports to be submitted for inclusion in the City Council agenda 14 days prior to the City Council
meeting date. In order to expediate inclusion of comments and recommendations from Public
Safety Commission to the City Council, staff recommended that the Public Safety Commission
meeting date be moved to the 3rd Monday of the month. Additionally, in order to reduce staff
overtime hours, a recommendation was made to change the meeting start time from 7 PM to 6
PM.

In order to streamline the recruitment process across all boards and commissions, the City
Managers Office is recommending that all term dates, including the Public Safety Commission,
begin on June 1 to align with the State mandated start date of the Library Board. Public Safety
Commission members would complete their current term on May 31 of their term end year or
when a new advisory board member is appointed.

THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN MARINO HEREBY ORDAINS AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. Article 08, Chapter II of the San Marino City Code is hereby amended as
follows as it pertains to the Planning Commission:

02.08.01: CREATION AND COMPOSITION:

There is hereby created a city Planning Commission which shall consist of five (5) members. Each
member shall be an elector of the City.

02.08.02: APPOINTMENT AND TERM:

The Planning Commission shall consist of five (5) members and two (2) alternates appointed by
the Mayor, with the approval of the Council. All members of the Planning Commission shall be
persons residing in the City. (Ord. 0-15-1300, 9-25-2015)

Members of the Commission shall serve a term of four (4) years, with terms commencing June 1
of the year of appointment; except, that of the commissioners first appointed, two (2) shall serve
terms of two (2) years and three (3) shall serve terms of four (4) years. Thereafter, all
commissioners shall serve a term of four (4) years and until a successor has been appointed.

Commencing with terms that begin on or after July 1, 2010, no commissioner may serve more than
two (2) consecutive terms; however, after waiting a period of at least two (2) years following the
end of the second consecutive term, a commissioner may be reappointed for not more than two (2)
additional consecutive terms. Alternates may serve an unlimited number of consecutive terms.

The Planning Commission shall take action by majority vote of those present and constituting a
quorum. A quorum shall consist of three (3) members, or member and alternates. An alternate shall
serve when any member is absent or has recused themselves from a specific case.

02.08.03: VACANCIES:

Vacancies to the Planning Commission shall be filled by appointment of the Mayor with the
approval of the Council, after providing for a twenty (20) day public notice period of such vacancy.
Appointment to fill a vacancy shall be for the remainder of the unexpired term.

The members of the Planning Commission shall select a chairperson and a vice chairperson from

Members of the Planning Commission shall serve without compensation.

approved by the Council.

02.08.06: MEETINGS:
